source.author: John Henry Comstock
source.credit: After Comstock 1918, The Wings of Insects, fig. 379 (scan leaf n402)

derivative.note: Centre-line tracing of a scanned printed figure (archive.org wingsofinsectsex00coms, PDF page 403); lines were found automatically (ridge filter, skeleton, smoothing) and are not redrawn by hand. No names are assigned. The print carries Comstock–Needham vein lettering; it is visible in the scan underneath but is not transcribed.
derivative.license: unknown (source is public domain; the licence of the EntoWing tracing has not been set)
derivative.attribution: John Henry Comstock (1918), fig. 379; tracing by EntoWing
derivative.precision: Douglas–Peucker 1.7 px on a 300 dpi scan, then Catmull–Rom smoothing; check against the scan

provenance.familyBasis: Tabanus is the type genus of Tabanidae.
provenance.letteringSystem: Williston's older vein and cell names (figure after Williston)
notes: Comstock's caption: 'Wing of Tabanus (After Williston)'. The print names cells and veins in Williston's older numbering (e.g. '1st posterior', '3rd vein'); these words are not transcribed.
Large cursive lettering crosses several cells; short ticks along the veins can be remnants of it.
